races.title: State Assembly, District 59
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Phillip Chen
cands.bio: Republican member of the California State Assembly, first elected in 2016 and now representing District 59. He owns a property management company with his mother. Earlier he served on the Walnut Valley school board, worked as a health deputy to an LA County supervisor, and was an LA County reserve sheriff's deputy.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed for 2026 and 2024)
California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO, and the National Union of Healthcare Workers (listed for 2026)

cands.gaps: We could not find where Phillip Chen was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found no statements from him on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice. We also found no documented deeds on those topics, apart from the two bills noted. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since 2016 (about ten years), with a stint as Deputy Whip of the Assembly Republican Caucus. Before that, Walnut Valley school board trustee from 2011 to 2016 and health policy advisor to the LA County Board of Supervisors. Also a property management business owner, USC adjunct professor and former reserve sheriff's deputy, with a master's in public administration and a doctorate in educational psychology.
qual.why: Roughly ten years of prior legislative service, plus local elected office, a policy-advisor career and business ownership, place him in the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget. Committee posts were not counted.
qual.label: Roughly ten years of prior legislative service, plus local elected office, a policy-advisor career and business ownership, place him in the high band for a job that writes law and the state budget. Committee posts were not counted.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Introduced AB 2021, which would have required the Department of Parks and Recreation to look for opportunities to acquire land to expand Chino Hills State Park. It passed the Water, Parks and Wildlife Committee unanimously but died in Appropriations.

back-police-order.evidence: Introduced AB 517 in 2019 to create a Property Crime Task Force in Orange County to identify and arrest people committing property crimes. The bill cleared the public safety committee and then died.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 2 backed by their record, 0 only promised

cands.name: Victor Hernandez
cands.bio: Green Party candidate for California State Assembly District 59. Born in Santa Ana and lives in Brea. He says he co-developed a low-cost mobile healthcare service with his wife. He served on the board of California United for Single Payer. He has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: He says the Peace and Freedom Party, Green Party of California and Green Party of Orange County endorsed him (self-reported in his Ballotpedia survey).

cands.gaps: We found no record of prior elected office or of his paid work history. We could not confirm the structure of the mobile healthcare service he says he co-developed, or his role in it. We found no stated positions on homestead property taxes, guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, police funding, H-1B visas, or limits on investor or foreign land buying. His statements on data centers and land are undated campaign-site text, and no specific legislation or actions were cited.

local.label: Roots 100: He says he was born and raised in Orange County, with his life beginning in Santa Ana, and his campaign site calls him a lifelong Orange County resident now living in Brea.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: His campaign site says he co-developed a low-cost mobile healthcare service with his wife and served on the board of California United for Single Payer. He has held no elected office, and no legislative, policy or budget career was found.
qual.why: No prior elected or legislative service was found, and the healthcare service's structure and his role in it are not documented. The nonprofit board seat adds nothing to the score, so this sits in the low range.
qual.label: No prior elected or legislative service was found, and the healthcare service's structure and his role in it are not documented. The nonprofit board seat adds nothing to the score, so this sits in the low range.

stop-data-centers.evidence: His campaign issues page lists "Place Moratorium on Hyperscale Data Centers" under protecting natural resources.

clean-money.evidence: He says he rejects donations from corporations, lobbyists and super PACs, and describes his campaign as 100% people-funded.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: He lists converting public lands to parks as a priority and says elected officials must be stewards of land, water, air and ecosystems.

workers-first.evidence: His issues page lists "Protect Immigrants Against ICE" and "Uphold Sanctuary Principles" among his priorities.
